method: Take curd in a jar.
Mix very well and make sure it is lumps-free.
Add salt as per taste.
Add chopped coriander.
Prepare the tadka: Heat oil, add rai and green chili. Once they splutter, pour the tadka over the curd mixture.
Pour the chaas (buttermilk) in glasses.
You can also chill the buttermilk in the refrigerator and serve later. But use it on the same day.
Take curd in a jar.
Just shake in the whisker for some minutes till everything is blended well.
Add water.
Add salt as per taste.
Pour chaas in glasses.
You can also chill the buttermilk in the refrigerator and serve later. But use it on the same day.
To begin making the Solkadhi Recipe, first take a vessel.
In a bowl, add water, coconut milk, kokum syrup, kokum agal, garlic ginger, green chili.
Stir well to mix and garnish with green coriander.
Then filter the above mixture.
Taste it and adjust seasoning as required. Garnish the Solkadhi with chopped coriander and serve chilled.
To begin making the Masala Kokam, first take a vessel.
In a bowl, add water, kokum syrup, kokum agal, garlic, ginger, and chili spice paste and stir well to combine.
If required, then filter the above mixture.
Taste it and adjust seasoning as required. Garnish the Masala Kokam with chopped coriander and serve chilled.
To begin making the Kokam, first take a vessel.
In a bowl, add water, kokum syrup, jeera powder, and salt and stir well to combine.
Taste it and adjust seasoning as required.
Serve chilled. No garnish required.
Mix shrikhand with curd and milk in a bowl and whisk well to make a lump-free mixture.
Add black pepper powder and cinnamon mix well.
Pour piyush in serving glasses.
Garnish with chopped badam.
Serve chilled. Keep the consistency of Shrikhand accurate.
Mix shrikhand with rose water and milk in a bowl and whisk well to make a lump-free mixture.
Add cinnamon and black pepper powder and mix it well.
Pour rose piyush in serving glasses.
Garnish with chopped badam / rose petal.
Serve chilled. Crush the rose petals on palms and then add these squeezed petals for garnishing.
Mix shrikhand with mango pulp and milk in a bowl and whisk well to make a lump-free mixture.
Pour mango piyush in serving glasses.
Garnish with chopped badam.
Serve chilled. Don't use Curd and Black pepper powder.
Take water in a container, add awala syrup in it.
Add salt and mix well.
Taste it and serve chilled.
First, cook the raw mango in a cooker for 2 whistles.
Then, once it cools down, take the pulp of the cooked raw mango and make a smooth puree with the help of a spoon.
Add sugar and salt.
Add water in it as per consistency required.
Serve chilled.
Slice the lemon and squeeze the juice with the squeezer or with the help of your hand into water. Discard the seeds. Add sugar, salt.
Take water in a vessel and ice cubes.
Mix all until sugar dissolves. Pour into tall glasses and add lemon slices if using.
Serve nimbu pani chilled.
Slice the lemon and squeeze the juice with the squeezer or with the help of your hand into water. Discard the seeds. Add sugar, salt. Take water in a vessel and ice cubes.
Mix all until sugar dissolves. Add jaljeera powder 2 tbsp. Mix everything well until the jaljeera powder is dissolved.
Now add ice cubes and serve it cool in a glass.
Boil water in a saucepan.
Add tea powder and boil it for 3-4 minutes on medium flame.
Add milk and boil it over medium flame for 6-7 minutes or until bubbles start to rise.
You will see the change in color of the tea from milky shade to brown shade when it is ready.
Turn off the gas and strain tea in cups. Adjust the tea powder as per requirement of strength.

ingredients: Salt: 1 teaspoon (or add as per taste)
method: Slice the onions thinly and place them in a mixing bowl or vessel. Add a pinch of salt and mango cut powder or lemon juice and mix it well.
Keep this bowl untouched for 5 minutes.
Add haldi powder, cumin powder, red chili powder, coriander leaves, water, besan, and salt.
Mix the besan, salt, and oil very well with your fingertips with the onions.
Allow the mixture to rest for 5 to 6 minutes, as the onions will release their moisture.
Heat oil for deep frying in a deep pan/vessel or kadai.
For crispy bhajis, ensure the oil is hot. Add a spoonful of the batter to the hot oil.
Fry the kandha bhajis on a medium flame, flip with slotted spoon.
Fry till they turn golden brown. Remove and place on absorbent kitchen napkins.
Serve kandhabhaji hot with fried green chilies, spicy green chutney. Sprinkle Chat Masala before serving.
Place the dal in a vessel and wash under running water and soak them for about 12 hours. Add black pepper.
Drain the excess water.
Place this soaked dal in a mixture blender.
Transfer this paste to a bowl and add onion, chopped green chili paste, jeera powder, cilantro, and salt. Mix well and make sure the batter is not too liquid.
Now, heat the oil in a wok, and when the oil is sufficiently heated, drop spoonfuls of the prepared batter and fry these vadas till golden brown and crisp.
Drain them on a plate lined with kitchen paper.
Serve hot with green chutney.
Take a bunch of coriander and clean it properly. Remove any yellow or rotten leaves.
Chop the stalks and leaves fine. Wash the coriander with water really well.
Remove any dirt or soil present in it. Spread the coriander on a towel or clean cloth and let it dry completely.
On the gas, put a kadhai on it. Let it get heated.
Put oil and after that add mustard seeds to get them crackle.
Add green chili paste and green chili chopped in the oil.
Mix all chopped dry fruits and khaskhas as well.
Next, add haldi and hing and sauté it very well.
Add coriander into the kadhai and cook well and lastly add salt to it.
Remove the above stuff into the pan and add hot water very slowly and in limited quantity.
Make the consistency a semi-gravy and add amchur powder to it.
Apply a little oil on a plate and spread the batter in the plate. Take a steamer and heat it up.
Keep the kothimbir vadi plate in the steamer. Steam the vadi on medium heat for about 15-20 minutes.
After steaming, take the vadi out and let it cool down. Cut the pieces into diamonds.
Heat up oil and drop square vadi into it.
Fry the vadi until light golden from both sides and take them out.
Sprinkle Chat Masala on it. Serve with Green Chutney or Tamarind Chutney.
Firstly, in a large kadai, make a masala. Put oil and mustard.
Add ginger paste, garlic paste, green chili paste, amchur powder, turmeric powder, jeera powder.
Add vada pav masala. After cooking the masala, add green peas paste.
After cooking, add fried besan. Add sugar and salt amchur to taste and mix.
KACHORI DOUGH RECIPE:
Firstly, in a large mixing bowl, add 250g maida, and Mohan oil and salt to taste, and water.
Crumble the flour well with oil.
In addition, add water little by little and knead to form a dough. Cover them for 15 mins with a wet cloth.
Now, scoop 1 tsp of prepared masala stuffing.
Get the edges together and form a bundle.
Furthermore, gently press the edges and flatten. Deep fry kachoris.
Then press with the spoon to puff up.
Finally, serve yummy kachori.
Mashed the boiled potato, mix with vadapav masala and salt, taste it and make 30 gm of vada.
Mix besan, flour, rice flour, turmeric powder, ajwain, and salt well and add water as per required.
Consistency of batter should be medium. Heat the oil in a kadhai for deep frying.
Dip the potato balls in the besan batter and deep fry them.
Served it with four green fried chilies.
First clean and wash Green coriander and green chilies.
Strain them well, make sure no water is present. Then grind both the ingredients in a pulverizer. No water.
Second, crush the whole dry coriander seeds in a cloth with the help of a hammer or dabhu, just to get a roughly coarse form.
Third, be ready with all ingredients.
Fourth, the entire masala should cook on low to medium flame. Keep proper control on the range flame.
Now heat oil in a kadhai. Put mustard seeds, let them splutter.
Add garlic paste, sauté. Add ginger paste, sauté well. Add turmeric powder, cumin powder, and coriander powder.
Sauté all the dry masala thoroughly. Avoid its burning.
Then add paste of Green chilies and green coriander. Sauté well on medium flame till the oil separates.
Finally, add salt and roughly coarse dry coriander. Mix well.
Allow it to cool down completely. Then store it in a dry container.
Soaked poha in water for 2-3 min.
Take a kadhai. Then add oil, shengadana, let it be crispy.
Then add rai, let it splutter.
Then add chopped green chili, curry leaves, sliced onion, sauté well.
Then add turmeric powder, sauté. Then add soaked poha and a pinch of salt, sugar, amchur powder. Mix well, cook.
Then add green coriander. Sprinkle some water, put the lid, keep it for 2 minutes.
Serve hot with Lemon Pc. Garnish with freshly grated wet coconut and coriander.

ingredients: 120 gm patal Poha (Flattened rice), thin variety
method: To begin making the Dadpe Pohe Recipe.
Dry the thin variety of poha or flattened rice and keep aside.
Now take a bowl, add the poha, add buttermilk, mix it well till it gets soggy.
Grated coconut, sugar, and salt. Mix buttermilk (if required) and mix well, with the hands. Leave it to soak.
Heat oil in a small tadka pan, add the mustard seeds, asafoetida, and let it crackle.
Add the green chili, Kaju, and saute.
Add this tadka over the softened poha and mix well.
At last, do micro oven for 1 minute.
To serve, take a portion of the prepared Dadpe Pohe in a plate, garnish with the grated coconut, coriander leaves.
If guest asks, then only serve with curd.

ingredients: 200 g Rice, soaked for 4 to 5 hours
method: For 1 pc of Ghavan, use 100 ml of batter.
To begin making the Maharashtrian Ghavan Recipe, soak the rice in water overnight or 5 to 6 hours.
Once soaked well, grind into a smooth thick batter. Add salt, jeera, coconut milk, and Rawa, adding little water at a time.
Water to adjust the consistency of the Ghavan to ensure it is not very thick nor very thin.
Cover the batter and keep it aside for 10 to 15 minutes.
Heat a non-stick tawa and spread a little oil on it. Stir the batter and pour the batter from the edge of the pan moving towards the center. Spread evenly. Reduce the heat.
Drizzle little oil all around and cook it until light brown. Now flip it and cook it on the other side too.
Transfer Ghavan on a serving plate and serve immediately.
Serve Maharashtrian Ghavan with green chutney. Serve 2 pc. No Buttermilk.

ingredients: Oil: for tadka and for deep frying the vadas
method: Place all the dal in a vessel and wash them under running water and soak them for about 3-4 hours. Drain the excess water.
Put this soaked dal overnight in a mixture blender and add chopped green chilies and ginger to it and blend them to form a coarse paste.
Transfer this paste to a bowl and add onion, coriander, and salt. Mix well and make sure the batter is not too dry; if it is, add 1-2 tablespoons of water.
Now pour the tadka on this batter of oil, hing, and chopped curry leaves. Mix well.
Now, heat the oil. Take batter in hand, make a small ball, flatten with palm, and make a tiny hole in the middle of the flattened ball and drop into oil. Fry these vada till golden brown and crisp.
Drain them on a plate lined with absorbent paper.
Serve hot with fried green chutney.
If the batter gets too loose, then add a little bit of besan for its binding.
Soaked green moong dal overnight.
Wash it nicely 2-3 times with water.
To make the pakoda batter, put split green gram in a mixer jar, add green chilies, ginger, garlic, and salt and grind into a coarse paste. Add a little water if required.
Transfer the batter into a mixing bowl, add all ingredients with besan, coriander leaves, and rice flour and mix well.
Using your fingers, drop small amounts of batter in hot oil and deep-fry till crisp and golden.
Arrange them on a serving plate and serve hot.
Serve with chat masala sprinkled on it.
Rinse the palak very well and finely chop them.
In a bowl, add the chopped palak leaves. Then add ginger and green chili paste, cumin powder.
Next, add besan, salt as per requirement. Mix all the ingredients very well and keep aside for 5 minutes.
Add water in parts. Remember the spinach will release water once they are mixed with salt and the spice powders. So be careful while adding water.
Mix very well. Add water as required to make a medium consistency pakoda batter.
For frying palak pakoda, heat oil in a kadai or pan. When the oil is medium hot, drop spoonfuls of the pakora batter in the oil.
Fry the pakora till they become pale golden. Then turn over and fry the other side.
Remove them with a slotted spoon. Drain them on a kitchen bowl. Serve palak pakoda hot with chutney.
First of all, make a lump-free mixture of besan and curd in a mixer, then add an equal quantity of water in it and keep aside.
Now in a kadhai, heat oil and add rai, let it splutter.
Then add methi dana, chopped green chilies, curry leaves, hing, and cloves and sauté it well.
Now add the above curd mixture over this tempering and give a stir.
Let it boil, mix well, and add water as per consistency.
Cook it thoroughly.
Finally, add lemon, ginger paste, ghee, salt, sugar, mix well, and cook it well, nicely boiling.
Taste it and serve warm.
In a kadhai, heat oil, add jeera and let it splutter, then add chopped green chilies.
Now add hing, turmeric powder, and add hot water in it to avoid its burning.
Once it boils, then add boiled toor dal.
Add water in it as per required consistency.
Finally, add salt and chop green coriander.
Boil it completely and taste it.
Serve hot.
In a kadhai, heat oil, add rai and let it splutter, then add chopped garlic, let it cook till it gets golden color.
Then add chopped green methi and sauté it well till its rawness is done.
Now add hing, turmeric powder, and add hot water in it to avoid its burning.
Once this water boils, then add boiled toor dal.
Add water in it as per required consistency.
Finally, add salt, sugar, amchur powder.
Boil it completely and taste it.
Serve hot.

ingredients: Green chop and boil palak: 150 gm
method: First boil the clean and chopped palak and strain it.
In a kadhai, heat oil, add rai and let it splutter, then add chopped garlic, let it cook till it gets golden color.
Now add hing, turmeric powder, and add hot water in it to avoid its burning.
Then add boiled palak and sauté it well.
Add water, let it boil, then add boiled toor dal.
Add water in it as per required consistency.
Finally, add salt, sugar, and Lemon.
Lastly, add coriander powder.
Boil it completely and taste it.
Serve hot.
In a kadhai, heat oil, add rai and let it splutter, then add chopped garlic, let it cook till it gets golden color.
Now add hing, turmeric powder and add hot water in it to avoid its burning.
Once it boils, then add boiled toor dal.
Add water in it as per required consistency.
Add tamarind pulp, jaggery, mix well.
Finally, add salt and chop green coriander.
Boil it completely and taste it.
Serve hot.
Grind all the above ingredients into a fine smooth paste.
Taste it and serve with snacks items.
Clean thoroughly the tamarind and keep it for boiling with almost double amount of water.
Once it gets thick, then allow it to cool down and strain well.
Now keep again to boil this strained tamarind puree.
Add jaggery, sugar and let it boil completely, then add washed groundnuts.
Finally, add clean sesame seeds.
Let it boil well.
Taste it and allow it to cool down completely.
Store it in a completely dry container in freeze.
Serve it with snacks.
In a bowl, mix all ingredients well and make a lump-free dry powder chutney.
Taste it and serve with vada pav and with batata vada.
Soak sabudana overnight or for 4-5 hours. Drain excess water.
Heat oil in a kadhai, add jeera and let it splutter.
Add chopped green chillies and sauté.
Add cubed boiled potatoes and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add soaked sabudana and mix gently.
Add peanut powder, salt, and sugar. Mix well.
Cook on low flame for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add lemon juice and garnish with coriander.
Serve hot.
Firstly, in a large bowl, take sabudana and soak with enough water for 3 hours.
Drain off the water and rest for 30 minutes, allowing to drain off the water completely.
Now take the soaked sabudana in a large bowl.
Also, add potato and peanuts.
Additionally, add 1 tsp cumin powder, salt.
Mix and mash well with your hand.
Prepare vada by deep frying.
Finally, serve sabudana vada hot along with curd.
6 pieces per plate.

ingredients: Chopped almonds and pistachios for garnish
method: Hang curd in a muslin cloth overnight to remove all whey.
Transfer the thick curd to a bowl.
Add powdered sugar and mix well until smooth.
Add cardamom powder and saffron strands.
Mix until creamy and smooth.
Garnish with chopped nuts.
Refrigerate and serve chilled.
Make sugar syrup with water and cardamom.
Mix khowa and maida to make smooth dough.
Make small balls from the dough.
Deep fry on low heat until golden brown.
Soak in warm sugar syrup for 2-3 hours.
Serve warm or cold.
In a kadhai, heat ghee and add aliv in it and sauté it till they crackle.
Then add water in it and cook it well.
Finally, add milk and sugar and cook well.
Taste it and serve it warm.
In a kadhai, heat ghee and add nachani flour and roast it well.
Then add milk and boil it.
Finally, add sugar and cook well.
Check the consistency and taste it.
And serve it warm.

ingredients: For covering: Maida 250gm, Oil 2 tbsp, Salt pinch, Water as required
For puran: Chana dal 250gm, Jaggery 300gm, Cardamom powder 1/2 tsp, Nutmeg powder 1/4 tsp
method: Make soft dough with maida, oil, salt and water. Rest for 30 mins.
Cook chana dal until soft. Drain and mash.
Add jaggery to mashed dal and cook until thick.
Add cardamom and nutmeg powder. Let it cool.
Make small balls of dough and puran filling.
Stuff puran in dough and roll into thin rotis.
Cook on tawa with ghee on both sides.
Serve hot with ghee.

ingredients: For covering: Rice flour 200gm, Water 300ml, Salt pinch, Oil 1 tsp
For stuffing: Fresh coconut grated 200gm, Jaggery 150gm, Cardamom powder 1/4 tsp
method: Boil water with salt and oil. Add rice flour and mix. Knead smooth dough.
For stuffing: Cook coconut and jaggery until thick. Add cardamom.
Make small cups from dough, fill with stuffing.
Shape into modak with pleats on top.
Steam for 10-12 minutes.
Serve hot with ghee.

notes: For Ekadashi and other fasting days
Full course meal with all accompaniments

tips: Use fresh spices for best flavor
Add hot water to avoid burning of masalas
Use proper thali plates for traditional service
